normative_text.rand.req.genl:
29.5.3.1 General requirements [rand.req.genl]
1
#
Throughout [rand],
where the template parameters are not constrained,
the names of template parameters are used to express type requirements
on an instantiated template T:
(1.1)
If T has a template type parameter named
    Sseq, URBG, Engine,
    RealType, IntType, or UIntType,
    the program is ill-formed if the corresponding template argument is cv-qualified.
(1.2)
A template argument corresponding to a template parameter
    named Sseq
    shall meet the requirements
    of seed sequence.
(1.3)
A template argument corresponding to a template parameter
    named URBG
    shall meet the requirements
    of uniform random bit generator.
(1.4)
A template argument corresponding to a template parameter
    named Engine
    shall meet the requirements
    of random number engine.
(1.5)
If a template argument corresponding to a template parameter
    named RealType
    is neither
    a standard floating-point type ([basic.fundamental]) nor
    a member of an
    implementation-defined subset of extended floating-point types,
    the program is ill-formed.
(1.6)
If a template argument corresponding to a template parameter
    named IntType
    is neither
    a standard signed nor a standard unsigned integer type ([basic.fundamental]), nor
    an extended integer type whose width is
    greater or equal to that of char and
    less than or equal to that of long long, nor
    a member of an
    implementation-defined
    subset of integer types, the program is ill-formed.
(1.7)
If a template argument corresponding to a template parameter
    named UIntType
    is neither
    a standard or extended unsigned integer type whose width is
    greater or equal to that of short and
    less than or equal to that of long long, nor
    a member of an
    implementation-defined
    subset of unsigned integer types, the program is ill-formed.
2
#
Throughout [rand],
phrases of the form “x is an iterator of a specific kind”
shall be interpreted as equivalent to the more formal requirement that
“x is a value
of a type meeting the requirements
of the specified iterator type”.
3
#
Throughout [rand],
any constructor that can be called with a single argument
and that meets a requirement specified in this subclause
shall be declared explicit.
